obligations: Share one color value with composed color controls.
Preserve accessible names for each child control.

behavior: Controlled and uncontrolled color strings are shared with children.
Does not participate in forms and admits no name; use a named ColorField to submit a color.

onChange emits a CSS string in the color space of the picker's value, or of its defaultValue when uncontrolled, whichever nested control made the edit: rgba(r, g, b, a) for hex and RGB values and hsla(h, s%, l%, a) for HSL and HSB values. With neither it emits rgba().

The picker converts every edit to that space and keeps its color there. A hex picker therefore reports rgba() after an edit from a nested ColorWheel, ColorField, or ColorSlider with colorSpace hsl, and an HSL picker reports hsla() after an edit from a nested ColorField or ColorSlider with colorSpace rgb.

A nested ColorArea, ColorField, or ColorWheel emits its own onChange in that space too. A ColorSlider with colorSpace set still emits its own onChange in that space, and a ColorSwatchPicker emits the chosen item's color.

The picker remembers the last edit of any nested control at full precision, including the hue that a hex or RGB value cannot hold for black, white, and grays. A hue ColorSlider therefore moves off a gray, and a ColorArea or ColorWheel then edits in that hue. The picker keeps the edit until a new value arrives that is not that edit's color; an alpha change and a value that has not yet caught up with the edit do not clear it.
disabled and readOnly on ColorPicker apply to the Mux UI color controls inside it: ColorArea, ColorField, ColorSlider, ColorSwatch, ColorSwatchPicker, and ColorWheel.
The flags reach those controls at any depth, through wrapper elements and fragments.
A child with disabled or readOnly set to false does not override a true flag on the picker.
Elements that are not Mux UI color controls, such as a native input, are not affected.
A disabled or read-only ColorPicker does not call onChange.
A ColorPicker with aria-label or aria-labelledby has the group role; without a name it is a plain wrapper.
